entry.title: Daily Briefing: September 24, 2026
entry.summary:
# Agent N's Hermes News — 24 September 2026

A big week for Hermes: the long-requested Bot Screen desktop passthrough finally shipped, Hermes Agent v0.21.4 landed a scripting-friendly CLI flag, the oh-my-hermes plugin ecosystem got a major upgrade, and the broader agent-runtime world moved around us. Here's what matters.

Releases

Bot Screen launches for Hermes Desktop. The week's dominant story: live desktop passthrough that lets you visually and interactively access the same machine your agent works on — and watch it drive a browser or terminal in real time. @Teknium and @NousResearch coordinated the launch, with an official @tonbistudio walkthrough and docs as the onboarding path. The lead post drew roughly 1,150 likes, and replies like "Finallllly!" plus a 20k-view "Much needed!" suggest this landed exactly as the community hoped.

Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21, released 21 Sep 2026) adds a --format stream-json CLI flag that emits structured JSONL — one JSON object per line. This is immediately actionable for automation, scripting, and integration workflows, and it's fresh news relative to this week's coverage.

oh-my-hermes (OMH) major update. @rlaope shipped Jev-Skills and model routing — Jev models and aliases, skills and plugins, workflow routing, fast decisions — positioning OMH as the all-in-one plugin for hermes-agent power users. Alongside it came the open-source jeval tool for Jev model evaluation and visualization, plus jev-ask and jev-XYZ skills in oh-my-hermes Updated+. (A duplicate share of jeval saw near-zero engagement — the original thread is the one to follow.)

Ecosystem releases worth tracking:

  • Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 (tagged 18 Sep 2026) hardens MCP security with sessions scoped per invocation — relevant to anyone running MCP servers or multi-agent stacks.
  • AgentProto v0.20.0 (22 Sep 2026) is a new Apache-2.0 TypeScript agentic runtime that lists Hermes as a supported agent.

Community

  • Official team responsiveness was on full display. @Teknium and @NousResearch stayed active in replies: directing a user to Hermes via iMessage with any model, correcting a misattribution (a tool credited to Anthropic is actually built by Nous Research), and triaging a reported cache bug by requesting reproducible steps. They also confirmed a community-reported issue was fixed. This support pattern is ongoing and reinforces trust around this week's launches.
  • Minor chatter: a lukewarm community take on Opus 5.5 vs Claude Code — notable mainly because Opus 5.5 GA'd on 22 September, the day before this coverage. There was also an open call for followers to share their GitHub builds.

Tips & Tutorials

  • Hermes-Claude subscription plugin, explained end to end. The deepest Hermes-specific editorial coverage this week: a walkthrough of the pipeline where Hermes drives a plugin that runs the unmodified official Claude Code CLI, paired with a security-focused companion piece on authentication. The auth model keeps credentials entirely with the official CLI via claude auth rather than API keys — directly addressing the top trust question for adopters. One caveat: all of this research-batch coverage comes from a single source (Julian Goldie), which concentrates rather than triangulates the narrative — cross-check against official docs before adopting.
  • Getting started with Bot Screen. The official @tonbistudio walkthrough and docs (548 likes on the post) are the canonical onboarding path.
  • Put --format stream-json to work. With one JSON object per line, Hermes Agent output drops cleanly into scripts, CI jobs, log parsers, and integration pipelines — no fragile regex scraping of terminal text required.

That's the batch. If you're running MCP servers, take a hard look at the Agent Framework 1.19.0 session-scoping changes — and if you've been waiting on Bot Screen, the docs are live.

entry.title: It's time! You can now access the same machine your Hermes Agent does visually and interactively wit...
entry.summary: Teknium announces that users can now visually and interactively access the same machine their Hermes Agent uses, via a live desktop passthrough supported on every remote gateway.

entry.title: Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin
entry.summary: Explains the Hermes Claude subscription plugin pipeline end to end: Hermes talks to the plugin, which drives the unmodified official Claude Code executable with conversation flowing as native stream-json, while Hermes retains its own loop, tools, approvals and compaction. Requirements are Hermes 0.21.4+ and Claude Code CLI 2.1.263 logged in. Each request spawns a fresh claude process in a private temp directory with native tools and skills disabled, and a per-request admission relay forwards exactly one upstream request, rejecting native retry attempts locally.

entry.title: Hermes Agent Stream JSON Output: New in v0.21.4
entry.summary: Documents Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (v2026.9.21), released 21 September 2026, which adds a --format stream-json CLI flag emitting structured JSONL (one JSON object per line) instead of plain text so scripts and pipelines can parse output reliably. Update paths include the hermes update command, the installer one-liner, or the nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.9.21 Docker image. The release also rolls up roughly 1,812 merged PRs including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency.

entry.title: Hermes-Claude Auth: How Login Works (No API Key)
entry.summary: Details the authentication model of the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: credentials belong entirely to the official Claude Code CLI via claude auth login, and the plugin never opens, copies, refreshes or prints credential files. No API key is required or sent; the plugin actively rejects inherited API-key, custom-endpoint and cloud overrides, naming conflicting variables without exposing values. Status checks are local (claude auth status reads the local store in about 0.3s), and separated setups can use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR.

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: What Changed
entry.summary: Covers the Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0 release tagged on GitHub 18 September 2026. Headline changes focus on MCP security: sessions scoped per invocation with requests authenticated against invocation identity, origin and ownership. Skill archives become ZIP-only with digest verification, ambiguous MCP configuration matches are rejected, and new vector-store connectors arrive for MongoDB, Azure DocumentDB and Azure Cosmos DB plus in-memory and portable filters. Breaking changes include deprecation of the MCP sampling callback.

entry.title: AgentProto Review: New Open Agent Runtime (2026)
entry.summary: Reviews AgentProto, an open-source Apache-2.0 TypeScript agentic runtime released 22 September 2026 (v0.20.0) that provides one interface to start, message, watch and stop any coding agent with quality gates before work lands. It integrates 14 agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, opencode and Mastra. The reviewer notes the project is very early, with single-digit GitHub stars and Tier 2 components labeled alpha scaffolding, concluding it is early-adopters-only.
